doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Rock era, electric piano, move east
title: Rock 'n' roll, the Beatles and the album 'Changes'
summary: Rock did not hurt their club work, but their manager wanted current songs, leading to 'Changes' and 'Grass'.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Did the advent of rock ‘n roll in the late 50s and early 60s affect what you did and how much you were able to do it?
It didn’t make too much of a dent because we still had the same clubs that we were working, and we could do repeats up in Buffalo, up in Toronto, Detroit, Baker’s Keyboard Lounge up there—

Except in one respect and that was recording. Because at that time we had a manager, what was his name — Monty Kaye was our manager. And Monty Kaye wanted us to incorporate some current music, like Beatles and stuff. Our daughters loved the Beatles and they listened to it, and when we first heard them we didn’t care for it much. As they went on they got better, and suddenly the tunes started coming through, the songs became better.
After a year and a half there was some great music that the Beatles wrote.
Yeah. And so we started listening a little more and we said well maybe. And then we picked out a bunch of things and did an album called — what was it called? I can’t think of the name of it now.

Yeah, “Changes” was I think the first one we did. And that was, we did a Phil Ochs’ tune, we did, what was the other guy, Donovan, and we did some Beatles things, some Lennon-McCartney tunes. And actually it was quite good. A lot of people still love that album. I mean I’ve had people tell me that they enjoyed it, especially younger people. And then the next one we did right after that was a thing called “Grass” and that was one that also had an electric piano, Roy played electric piano for a while because we thought it would be fun to try it.
